kind: assumed inputs; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository

independent_agents.note: Agents that answer yes or no independently, each with the same yes probability. The width table uses an observed share of one half, the share at which the exact interval is widest.

coverage_grid.note: Yes probabilities at which the coverage of the exact interval for 14 agents is checked.

shared_cause_model.note: Assumed generating model, not estimated from any project record. On each occasion one shared signal is drawn: yes with probability p. Each agent, independently of the others, copies the shared signal with probability c and otherwise decides alone: yes with probability p. Every agent then says yes with probability p, and the answers of two agents have correlation rho = c * c, so c = sqrt(rho).

simulation.note: Seeded simulation of the shared-cause model for one group size. One occasion is one shared signal and one answer per agent. One seed per correlation, used with random.Random(seed).

second_model.note: A second assumed generating model with the same pairwise correlation, used only to show which results depend on the choice of model. On each occasion a shared level q is drawn from a Beta distribution with parameters a = p * (1 - rho) / rho and b = (1 - p) * (1 - rho) / rho, whose mean is p; every agent then says yes with probability q, independently of the others. The answers of two agents have correlation 1 / (a + b + 1) = rho. The number of yes follows a beta-binomial distribution, computed here with exact fractions.

measurement_plan.note: Sizing of the measurement the lesson asks for. The simulated occasions of each correlation are cut into consecutive logs of the stated length; each log gives one estimate of the pairwise correlation. A log is said to show a shared cause when its estimate exceeds the 95th percentile of the estimates from the logs simulated with correlation 0.

panel_sizing.note: The same assumed model, yes probability and correlations at the size of the tribunal panel that observed-input.json describes, to size a log of panel verdicts. The number of agents is checked against the snapshot. Assumption: each persona's answer is reduced to two values (pass, or anything else), although the panel allows three. This fixture did not run the panel; none of these numbers is a measurement of it. One seed per correlation, and four times the occasions of the main simulation, because the share of logs that detect a weak correlation moves by several points from one run of 50,000 occasions to the next; the log lengths and the false-alarm rate are those of measurement_plan.

imaginary_cases.note: Cases the lesson discusses. None of them was observed.

unanimous_group.description: Every agent of the group says yes.

dashboard_claim.description: A dashboard reports that 12 of 14 agents approve and calls it a strong consensus.

precision_target.description: A team wants the aggregate share to fall within 5 points of the long-run rate on 95% of occasions.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical review board for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
